account: Researchers at the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL), the Max Planck Institute of Biophysics and collaborating institutions used AlphaFold and RoseTTAfold to predict structures of nuclear-pore proteins. They used ColabFold to model complexes and fitted the predictions to electron-microscopy maps. Their model covered more than 90% of the scaffold, roughly twice the coverage of the previous model. The authors checked the predictions against existing and new experimental structures. The work appeared as a preprint on 27 October 2021 and in Science in June 2022. An independent Harvard group used the same mix of cryo-electron microscopy and AlphaFold to build an almost full model of the frog nuclear pore's cytoplasmic ring, published in Science on 10 June 2022. The human models were released in the Protein Data Bank in 2022: the constricted-state model as entry 7R5K on 22 June and the dilated-state model as entry 7R5J on 21 September. In a 2023 review, Gaoxingyu Huang, Chao Zeng and Yigong Shi of Westlake University credit machine-learning structure prediction for nuclear pore complex models of unprecedented accuracy, and they cite this study.

ai_role.statement: AI structure prediction generated the nucleoporin and subcomplex models that formed the input to integrative modeling. The authors state that the predictions were benchmarked against existing and new experimental structures. The resulting model was validated against earlier and new experimental data, so the AI output was independently checked rather than accepted as given.

fields.title: AI-based structure prediction doubled structural coverage of the human nuclear pore complex scaffold

fields.account: Researchers at the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL), the Max Planck Institute of Biophysics and collaborating institutions used AlphaFold and RoseTTAfold to predict structures of nuclear-pore proteins. They used ColabFold to model complexes and fitted the predictions to electron-microscopy maps. Their model covered more than 90% of the scaffold, roughly twice the coverage of the previous model. The authors checked the predictions against existing and new experimental structures. The work appeared as a preprint on 27 October 2021 and in Science in June 2022. An independent Harvard group used the same mix of cryo-electron microscopy and AlphaFold to build an almost full model of the frog nuclear pore's cytoplasmic ring, published in Science on 10 June 2022. The human models were released in the Protein Data Bank in 2022: the constricted-state model as entry 7R5K on 22 June and the dilated-state model as entry 7R5J on 21 September. In a 2023 review, Gaoxingyu Huang, Chao Zeng and Yigong Shi of Westlake University credit machine-learning structure prediction for nuclear pore complex models of unprecedented accuracy, and they cite this study.

echoes.setting: Harvard Medical School and Boston Children's Hospital: cryo-EM of the Xenopus laevis nuclear pore cytoplasmic ring combined with AlphaFold predictions of each nucleoporin gave an almost full atomic model of the ring.

purpose: Predict protein and subcomplex structures to enable integrative modeling of a 120-MDa macromolecular machine that resisted conventional structural biology.

ratings.reason: The collaborating laboratories obtained a model that roughly doubles the structural coverage of the human nuclear pore complex scaffold. That is a material advance for the research programs of those groups.
A 70-MDa atomically resolved model covering over 90% of the scaffold is a durable public resource for nuclear transport research. The source reports no direct patient or population benefit.
